questions.question: What phonon-mode reinterpretation does the paper advance for ZnTe₁₋ₓSeₓ?

options.A: A percolation-type 1-bond→2-mode description analogous to InGaAs and InGaP
options.B: A strict VCA 2-bond→1-mode description with no local environments
options.C: A 2-bond→2-mode model driven only by LO polarization
options.D: A 1-bond→1-mode model in which both bond species share one oscillator

questions.rationale: The authors argue ZnTeSe joins a universal percolation class visible in TO spectroscopy.
questions.evidence_quote: Here we show that the latter alloy obeys the same phonon mode behaviour as the former two, thereby a universal one, of a percolation type (1-bond→2-mode).

questions.question: Why does the authors' mesoscopic percolation model split a bond-related TO branch?

options.A: Like bonds vibrate differently in B-rich and C-rich regions because their local distortions differ
options.B: The TO band splits whenever the lattice is polar, independent of composition
options.C: The split is caused by the acoustic branch crossing a Brillouin-zone boundary
options.D: Different isotopes create two masses for each bond type

questions.rationale: Distinct local bond distortions in the two regional environments produce the double branch.

questions.question: What three-oscillator assignment do the authors propose for ZnTeSe TO modes?

options.A: One Zn–Te branch below two Zn–Se branches associated with Se-rich and Te-rich regions
options.B: Two Zn–Te branches above one Zn–Se branch
options.C: One Zn–Se branch and two collective LO modes
options.D: Three Zn–Te branches generated by separate isotopic environments

questions.rationale: The Zn-Se double branch reflects two regional environments, while Zn-Te remains effectively unsplit.

questions.question: What fitted or inferred impurity-mode parameters does the paper report for Zn–Te and Zn–Se, respectively?
questions.rationale: The Te bond behaves nearly one-mode, whereas the Se branch has a finite splitting.
questions.evidence_quote: The (ωimp, ∆) values for the Zn-Te and Zn-Se bonds are (∼189 cm−1, ∼0 cm−1) and (∼195 cm−1, ∼8 cm−1), respectively.

questions.question: How did the authors estimate the Zn–Te and Zn–Se impurity-mode frequencies rather than directly calculating them?

options.A: They used EXAFS bond lengths and the pure-crystal TO Grüneisen parameters; direct LDA frequencies were avoided due to overbinding
options.B: They fit LO Raman linewidths and ignored bond lengths because EXAFS was unavailable
options.C: They inferred them from the percolation thresholds alone
options.D: They used the two-impurity supercell frequency without any correction

questions.rationale: Bond-length shifts translated to frequency shifts via γ, avoiding the LDA bias in direct impurity frequencies.

questions.question: What evidence fixed ΔZn–Se near 8 cm⁻¹?

options.A: A rescaled-MREI curve was fitted to the dominant Zn-Se branch in the continuum regime at large Se content
options.B: The Zn-Te data were fitted at the dilute Se limit
options.C: A first-principles calculation of a pure ZnSe crystal yielded 8 cm⁻¹
options.D: The 60-μm-like far-IR resonance set the value

questions.rationale: The dominant Se-rich branch's continuum-regime fit set the Zn-Se split; other branch pieces were inferred.

questions.question: Why can LO spectra misleadingly resemble a one-mode alloy even when TO modes expose percolation splitting?

options.A: The electric field couples close-frequency LO oscillators and channels much of their strength into a giant LO+ mode
options.B: LO vibrations have no restoring force in polar crystals
options.C: The LO modes are experimentally inaccessible at all compositions
options.D: The local bond distortions vanish for longitudinal motion

questions.rationale: Strong field-mediated coherence merges the apparent LO behavior, masking the TO double-branch structure.

questions.question: Which computational setup supplied an independent check on the predicted TO density of states?

options.A: A fully relaxed 32-atom supercell near x≈0.5 using plane-wave pseudopotentials, LDA, and linear response
options.B: A 64-atom Siesta cell at the dilute limit using only classical molecular dynamics
options.C: A 2-atom primitive cell treated with a tight-binding force field
options.D: A 32-atom unrelaxed supercell at x=0 using Hartree–Fock

questions.rationale: The zone-center TO-DOS calculation independently showed three oscillators at representative mid-composition.
questions.evidence_quote: in a fully-relaxed 32-atom supercell (volume and internal coordinates) at the representative composition x∼0.5

questions.question: What systematic discrepancy separates the calculated ZC TO-DOS from the phenomenological Raman lineshape?

options.A: The DOS is blue-shifted by about 20 cm⁻¹, attributed to LDA overbinding
options.B: The DOS is red-shifted by about 20 cm⁻¹ because Raman samples finite wavevectors
options.C: The DOS has only two peaks, while Raman has three
options.D: The DOS is composition-independent, unlike all Raman branches

questions.rationale: The authors attribute a slight overall blue shift to the known LDA overbinding tendency.

questions.question: What are the paper's two percolation thresholds for the minor Zn–Te and Zn–Se bond networks?

options.A: xB=0.19 for minor A–B bonds and xC=0.81 for minor A–C bonds
options.B: xB=0.81 for Zn–Te and xC=0.19 for Zn–Se
options.C: Both bond networks percolate at x=0.5
options.D: Zn–Te percolates at x=0 and Zn–Se at x=1

questions.rationale: The threshold labels and values mark when each minor bond species becomes connected across the lattice.
